beats.text: For ten years, Rama, Sita and Lakshmana wandered from ashram to ashram. Then they met the great Sage Agastya.
He guided them to Panchavati, a lovely land beside the Godavari river.
It was named for its five great banyan trees. Lotus ponds shone, and peacocks danced on the banks.
On the way, they met an old vulture, Jatayu, who said he was a friend of their father. 'I will guard Sita when you are away,' he promised.
Lakshmana built a simple cottage of leaves and bamboo, with clay walls and a floor of sacred grass.
For a while, they lived in peace. Deer came close. Birds sang at dawn. Winter came, and Rama and Lakshmana bathed in the cold river at first light.
These were the happiest days of their exile. But a storm was already on its way.
